answer: A TEE quote travels with each submission; the vendor root is checked before scoring, so an unquoted claim never reaches the ledger. Reward drops one unit per claim no auditor re-checked, which prices lazy prose directly. Stored text is compared by replay, so a duplicate is caught at the second copy, not the name. A pearl of a clean quote still loses value when half the claims go unchecked, and the jetty of the vendor root is the single point that, if it moves, forces every quote under it to be read again. A knoll of 3 auditors covers 40 claims an epoch, and beyond that the cut eats the reward.
